title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K: fixed-size window, add right, subtract left.
shortTitle: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K: Fixed-Size Window, Add Right, Subtract Left
keyPoints: The fixed-size sliding window finds the maximum sum among all contiguous subarrays of length K in O(n) time.
Compute the sum of the first K elements as the initial window, then slide by adding the entering element and subtracting the leaving one.
Each slide changes only two terms, making it O(1) per step instead of O(K) for recomputing from scratch.
The improvement over brute force is the reuse of overlapping work: O(n) vs O(n * K).
If K is larger than the array, there is no valid window; return a sentinel or throw.
Use long or BigDecimal for the accumulator to avoid overflow on large financial totals.
Negative values are fine because the window width is fixed; there is no benefit to dropping a prefix.

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a running window sum by adding the entering element and subtracting the leaving one, and track the maximum.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Fixed-size sliding window** – finds the maximum sum among all contiguous subarrays of length K.
- **Slide operation** – `windowSum += a[right] - a[right - K]` adds the new element and removes the old in one step.
- **O(n) time, O(1) space** – each slide is constant time; the whole scan visits each element once.
- **Improvement** – brute force recomputes each window from scratch in O(K), giving O(n * K) total.
- **Guard** – if K > array length, no valid window exists.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India wants the three-day stretch with the highest total deposits this week. Rajesh totals the first three days, then for each new day he adds that day and removes the day that slid out of the window, always remembering the biggest three-day total he has seen.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The maximum sum subarray of size K asks for the largest total among all contiguous windows of a fixed length, and the fixed-size sliding window solves it in O(n) time. First add up the first K elements for the initial window, then slide one position at a time, adding the entering element and subtracting the leaving one in a single O(1) operation.

The key efficiency point is the reuse of overlapping work. Brute force recomputes each window from scratch at O(K) per window, giving O(n * K). The sliding window changes only two terms per slide, making the whole scan linear. That reuse is the entire reason the technique exists.

Always guard against K being larger than the array (no valid window), and accumulate in a wide type like long or BigDecimal to avoid overflow on large financial totals. Negative values cause no trouble because the width is fixed and there is no reason to drop a prefix.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, this finds each customer's best K-day deposit streak to time a loyalty offer, running in linear time even over long deposit histories.

Remember one sentence: Slide a fixed-size window by adding the entering element and subtracting the leaving one, tracking the maximum sum in O(n) time.
